paper text.text:
We now determine the possible forms of $B$.
Lemma~\ref{core:retained-subdivision} applies with $B$,
$\{a,b,c,d\}$ and $\{ac,cd,db\}$ in the roles of $B$,
$A$ and $E$. The graph $B+ac+cd+db$ is a nonplanar,
$K_5$-minor-free minor of $G$, using the paths through
$p,q,r,z$ and $P_x$. Every $K_{3,3}$ subdivision in it uses
$cd$, since $B+ac+bd$ is planar. The retained minor is $B$
itself, since every allowed operation makes $B+ac+cd+db$ planar.
Shortening $P_w$ to $ef$ also gives a minor of $G$, so the resulting
graph consisting of $\Psi_1$ and $B$ has no $K_5$ minor.
With these conditions, three-connectivity of $B\cup K_4[\{a,b,c,d\}]$
and the minimality conditions above,
Construction~\ref{common:marked-construction} leaves
nine labeled bridges, five up to interchanging $A_1$ and $A_2$~\supp{E8}.

\begin{proposition}\label{dis:type-b-reduction}
If $G$ has a bridge of type (b) with at least two interior
vertices, then $G\cong\mathfrak{T}_{66}$, or there are two
twin pairs with disjoint neighborhoods and connecting paths
of minimum total length for which one of the following holds.
The bridges and their types are defined using these twins and paths.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item All three paths are edges.
\item There is a bridge of type (c) with at least two interior vertices.
\item Every bridge with nonempty interior has three attachments.
\end{enumerate}
\end{proposition}
\begin{proof}
Use Lemma~\ref{dis:type-b-forms}. The two single-edge exterior
alternatives give only $\mathfrak{T}_{66}$ in the enumeration~\supp{E8}. It remains to treat

B + K4[a,b,c,d].meaning: B plus all six edges among a, b, c, d

B + cd.meaning: B + cd, a subgraph of G since P_x = cd

Psi1 + B.meaning: the graph consisting of Psi_1 and B, with P_x = cd and P_w shortened to ef: twins p, q on {a, c, e} and r, z on {b, d, f}, where e = s_w, f = t_w

vertex names: the attachments a = s_m, b = t_m, c = s_x, d = t_x of B; interior vertices of B are u0, u1, ...; for the bridges that pass, the paper's names are given with the verdict

excluded by a hypothesis of the case.fact: an interior vertex of degree three has two adjacent neighbours
excluded by a hypothesis of the case.why it excludes the bridge: Lemma 3.3(a); the edges added in the test graph are edges of G.
The proof shows: "The graph B + ac + bd is planar."

excluded by a hypothesis of the case.fact: B plus all edges among a, b, c, d has a cut of at most two vertices
excluded by a hypothesis of the case.why it excludes the bridge: Three-connectivity of B ∪ K_4[{a,b,c,d}], used with Construction 3.16.

verdicts.K5 minor: a K5 minor in the named graph, which is a minor of G
verdicts.proper nontoroidal minor: an allowed reduction of B (Section 3) after which the named test graph is still nonplanar; the proof shows that this gives a proper nontoroidal minor of G
verdicts.isomorphic to a bridge given in the text: B passes every test of the case and is isomorphic to a bridge given in the text (listed under "bridges given in the text"); the record that it passes the tests is kept with the verdict

whole graphs: For each bridge that passes, the two graphs of Lemma 4.30(i): G = (Psi_1 ∪ B) + eb and G = (Psi_1 ∪ B) + af, with P_x = cd and P_w = ef. Proposition 4.31 cites this part for the claim that these give only T66. The exterior formed by a bridge uv on {c,d,e,f} is treated in the paper by argument, so it is not included here.
